Source class reject_flue_clean (note 23, decided 2026-10-02). The condensing increment only, 0.05 of fuel energy in. A standard feedwater economiser is taken as already inside the boiler's efficiency ([DOE_WHR2008] appendix table: 75% of US boiler capacity is assumed to have one), so this row carries only what a condensing economiser adds on top. [DOE_STEAM26A] p.1 puts a condensing economiser's gain at 'up to 10%', which includes the feedwater step; [BREF_ENE2009] section 3.2.5 puts that step at 4 to 4.5 points (its example, 80% to 84.5%), leaving about 5.5; taken as 0.05, below the 6 to 8 points of [ACEEE_SCHIFFHAUER2009]'s case study. The heat is recovered below the flue gas water dew point (about 57 C for natural gas, [DOE_STEAM26A] p.1), so no warmer than heat_lt60. The practical limit sits in this row; economiser_flue_condensing draws it at 1.0. 0.05 x -1.13636 = 0.05682 per unit of output, within the unit's losses (note 20 item 70). Replaces a value from [DECC_SURPLUSHEAT2014]'s (48 - 13)/291 = 0.12027, which is rejected non-solid heat as a share of UK industrial energy (section 5, p.24, not section 4.1 as this row once cited), not a recoverable fraction: the report's technical, economic and commercial potentials are 11, 7 and 5 TWh/yr of those 35
